I have a G26 and I love it for CCW, but I've been thinking about getting a G30. I've heard that despite the big round in a small package, it is more of a "push back" rather than a "kick" recoil and is surprisingly easy to control. Was wondering if anyone could corroborate that. I've shot a G27 and felt that it was slightly too much "kick" for a subcompact, or at least I preferred the G26 for quicker, more accurate shot placement, but that is just me.
Any of you guys own or ever shot a Glock 30 (.45 subcompact Glock)

I've shot glock 27s, haven't shot a glock 30 yet. Oddly enough the last time I went shooting I found a full mag for a glock 30 on the ground in the woods. Someone must have dropped it in the snow I guess.
Glocks don't fit my hands really well, but I found I liked the G30 and the G26 fine. I don't like .40sw in almost any platform.

I felt the same about glocks until someone who wears one for a living explained to me the grip shape is intentionally like that for fast target acquisition. He reluctantly went from his high end 1911s to Glock earlier that year because he believes in them as a tactical pistol. I didn't believe it and was about to sell my glocks to change to Sig or SW so I did many tests of drawing a pistol up to a target repeatedly with different makes and models of pistols. I could t believe wha to found, which was for me, when I drew up the more comfortable gripped pistols, the natural position of the front site was inconsistent. When I drew up the glocks, they were naturally on target and much more consistent. After that I committed to Glock and haven't looked back. After using them and knowing why the grip was made the way it was, I've become acclimated to the shape and it feels great to me now. No one needs to agree with me, just sharing my experience.

I rock a G 30SF. 3.5 trigger upgrade. Best CCW platform bar none imo. Double taps, "if your into that kind of thing" at 10' are overlaps, keyholes not uncommon, considering the round equals impressive for certain.
It is significantly heavier and thicker, I owned one for a while and I felt like my 19 was more concealable.

G19: 670 g (855 g loaded) G19 Gen4: 670 g G30: 750 g G30SF: 745 g G30S: 650 g (860 g loaded)

As you can see, G30S is about as heavy as G19, while the older members of the family are quite a bit heavier. That is why G30S exists: the original G30 was a sawed-off G21, G30SF was G30 with the slide of G36, and G30S is G30SF on a radical diet.

In any incarnation, G30 is significantly thicker than G19, even with the G36 slide, although the thinner slide helps in some situations (e.g. IWB).

I have a .45 ACP revolver that weighs about the same as G30S or Springfield XD-S. Shooting that or XD-S is not particularly pleasant. Interestingly enough, Springfield's XD Mod.2 is very similar to original G30, even a little heavier, despite being newer than G30S. I would say if you're concerned about the recoil, and you insist on carrying a subcompact .45, you have to eat the weight penalty somehow. Like maybe using a shoulder rig and chuck a Mod.2 in there.

The G30 is much bigger than the G26. It's closer in size to a G19 but thicker. For recoil, if you felt a 27 was too snappy you likely would not like the G30s which has a thinner and lighter slide than the more manageable G30. It's basically the single stack g36 slide on a g30 frame for more capacity. I know people who swear by the G30 and the G30s and the G36. You need to go shoot them to know if the recoil (and ammo cost of .45) is acceptable to you. If you train it gets easier.
